card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. She trained and worked as a florist, but the independent flower shop she worked at in Castleford closed about eighteen months ago and she hasn't had a job since. She does occasional unpaid flowers for friends' and family's weddings and does online surveys for pocket money.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Pontefract. Level 2 and Level 3 diplomas in floristry at a further education college in Wakefield, done part-time while working in the shop. She started an online Level 3 course in wedding planning but never finished it.
card.household: Lives with her husband Craig (29), a shift supervisor at a distribution warehouse off the M62, in a two-bedroom ex-council semi they bought three years ago. No children yet. They have an anxious rescue whippet called Mabel. Craig's job and pay are what keep them in a C1 household.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in West Yorkshire. Her mum is a dinner lady and her dad drove for a builders' merchant until his knees went. Her grandad worked at one of the local pits before the closures, which still comes up at family dos. She isn't religious. She got married at the registry office in Wakefield with a do afterwards at a local cricket club. She's close to her mum and her younger sister, who live ten minutes away.
card.professional_persona: Careful and gentle with customers. At the shop she was the one who dealt with sympathy flowers, because she was patient with people who were upset. She's good with her hands and has a decent eye for colour, but she's disorganised with orders, paperwork and invoices, and the old owner used to do all that side. Being out of work has knocked her confidence. She finds job interviews and phoning places very stressful, and she tends to put applications off.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Mabel round the park and along the lanes most days, but slowly. She went to a beginners' Pilates class twice and stopped going because she felt self-conscious. Craig watches rugby league (Castleford Tigers) and she sometimes sits with him for it.
card.arts_persona: Likes pretty, hands-on things rather than galleries. She follows florists and pressed-flower artists on Instagram and Pinterest. She watches comfort telly like Bake Off and Gilmore Girls rewatches, and she reads cosy mysteries on her Kindle. She went to Yorkshire Sculpture Park once with her sister and liked the walk more than the sculptures.
card.travel_persona: A homebody who gets anxious about travelling. Holidays are usually a static caravan at Filey or a cottage in the Dales that takes dogs. She's been abroad a few times: Benidorm with friends at 19, and Tenerife for the honeymoon, which she enjoyed but was nervous about flying for. She'd like to see Amsterdam for the flower markets but hasn't got round to planning it.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking. Tea is things like spag bol, chicken fajitas from a kit, sausage and mash, or a chippy tea on Fridays. Sunday dinner at her mum's most weeks, with Yorkshire puddings. She bakes when she's stressed, mostly traybakes and banana bread from Instagram recipes, though they don't always turn out. She drinks a lot of tea and the odd pink gin.
hobbies_and_interests: pressing flowers and making little framed pieces for friends
scrolling florist and home decor accounts
tending a few pots and a small raised bed in the back garden
skills: calming down upset or nervous people
card.career_goals: Vague and a bit stalled. She'd like to do wedding and funeral flowers from home as a small business one day, but the thought of setting up a website, doing the accounts and putting herself out there puts her off. In the meantime she's half-heartedly looking at part-time jobs in garden centres or supermarket floral departments.
card.voice: Quiet, soft West Yorkshire accent: short vowels in 'bath' and 'grass', and flattened 'u' in words like 'love' and 'mum'. She talks fairly slowly and often trails off at the end of sentences. She says 'erm' a lot and hedges with 'sort of' and 'I don't know, it's just...'. She'll say 'tea' for her evening meal, 'mum', and occasionally 'love' or 'you was' without thinking. She apologises often ('sorry, that probably doesn't make sense') and will agree with the interviewer to be nice. She doesn't fill silences herself. She waits, or gives a little laugh, and needs gentle prompts to expand. She opens up a bit more when talking about flowers or the dog.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with capitals only sometimes at the start. Few full stops, and she'll string things together with commas or 'and'. Apostrophes are often missing ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Short answers. She uses the odd 'lol' or 'tbh', and sometimes ends with '...' if she's unsure. No emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Shy and polite, slightly nervous at first, smiles a lot and keeps answers short. She's very agreeable and won't contradict anyone, so she can come across as having fewer opinions than she really has. Warm once she relaxes. She'll ask the other person if they're alright and thank them more than once.
small_things: Mabel being scared of the bin lorry
a cosy murder mystery she's halfway through
the peonies in her garden coming through
Craig being on nights this week
a banana bread that sank in the middle
deeper_things: She feels guilty and a bit useless about not working while Craig does long shifts
She gets bad anxiety and has thought about seeing the GP about it but keeps putting it off
She's unsure whether she wants children soon, and people keep asking
She was really upset when the flower shop closed, because it felt like her place
She worries she's not organised enough to ever run her own business
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop camera angled slightly upward, so the ceiling corner is visible. Soft, slightly grey daylight from a window to her left, leaving the right side of her face a little shadowed. She is a young white woman with a round face, light freckles, pale skin and minimal makeup, smiling slightly with closed lips and looking a bit shy, eyes just off the camera. Shoulder-length mousy blonde hair is pulled back in a loose claw clip, with strands falling around her face. No glasses. She wears an oversized sage-green knitted jumper and has a small silver necklace. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall in a small living room. A grey fabric settee is partly visible with a mustard throw over the arm, and a whippet curled up asleep on a cushion. A white shelf on the wall holds two small framed pressed-flower pictures, a trailing pothos plant and a candle in a jar. A wedding photo in a silver frame sits slightly out of focus at the edge of the frame.
